title: From Financial Dependence to Self-Employment: Suji K.P.’s Journey of Empowerment
body_text:
For women from economically constrained families, skills alone may not be sufficient to create sustainable livelihoods. Timely access to affordable credit can help them establish enterprises, earn independently and strengthen their families’ financial security.
Demonstrating the impact of support under the NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme, Suji K.P., a resident of Wayanad district in Kerala, transformed her tailoring skills into a viable enterprise and moved from financial dependence towards self-reliance.
Suji belongs to the OBC Hindu Thiyya community. Before receiving assistance, she had no independent source of income and was financially dependent on her husband, whose earnings were the primary source of livelihood for the family.
Although Suji possessed tailoring skills and wished to start her own business, limited family income made it difficult to arrange the capital required for machinery, materials and other essential business needs.
The major barrier in her journey was economic. Her loan applications were rejected by conventional banks because she had no personal earnings and the family had limited financial resources. As a result, she was unable to establish a tailoring unit despite having the required skills and determination.
Suji aspired to become financially independent by setting up her own tailoring unit. She wanted to create a sustainable source of income, contribute to household expenses and provide greater financial security to her family.
It proved turning point when Suji attended an awareness programme organised by the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC). Through the programme, she learned about the financial assistance available under the NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme. And, in 2023, Suji received a loan of ₹ 3,00,000 under the NBCFDC Schemethat enabled her to establish a tailoring unit and convert her existing skills into a dependable livelihood.
Suji subsequently expanded the enterprise by adding photocopy and lamination services. The diversification helped her cater to a wider range of customers, improve the viability of the unit and build a steadier source of income.
Before receiving the loan, Suji had no independent source of income. Today, she earns approximately ₹15,000 per month through her enterprise, marking a significant improvement in her economic position.
The steady income has reduced her financial dependence on her husband and strengthened the family’s financial security. It has also given her greater confidence, dignity and an identity as a self-employed entrepreneur.
The NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme enabled Suji to overcome the financial barrier that had prevented her from starting a business. Access to institutional credit helped her translate her skills and aspirations into sustainable self-employment.
Suji K.P.’s journey from having no independent income to running a multi-service enterprise reflects the transformative potential of timely financial assistance. Her success demonstrates how access to credit can empower women from economically constrained communities to build secure livelihoods and contribute meaningfully to their families.
SS-48-TAR-KV-GA-RK Date: 24.8.26

enrichment.summary: This PIB release profiles Suji K.P., a woman from Wayanad, Kerala, who used a ₹3,00,000 loan under the NBCFDC Self-Employment Scheme in 2023 to set up a tailoring unit after being rejected by conventional banks. She later diversified into photocopying and lamination services and now earns about ₹15,000 per month, achieving financial independence from her husband's income.
enrichment.context:
The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) is a Government of India undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment that provides concessional credit to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and similar economically weaker groups for self-employment ventures, often channelled through state-level agencies like the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC). Such schemes aim to address the credit gap faced by marginalized groups who are typically excluded from formal banking due to lack of collateral or credit history, thereby promoting entrepreneurship-led social and economic empowerment.

This release is a human-interest success story used by PIB to publicize the scheme's on-ground impact rather than an announcement of new policy or data. While NBCFDC itself is a recurring subject in socio-economic empowerment discussions, this particular piece offers no new statistics, policy change, or scheme modification — it simply illustrates an individual beneficiary's journey.
